text: Order these couplings from weakest to strongest: extending a class, a `List` parameter, shared mutable static state, a `new` call on a collaborator.
choices: `List` parameter, extending a class, `new` call, shared mutable static state.
Extending a class, `new` call, `List` parameter, shared mutable static state.
`List` parameter, `new` call, extending a class, shared mutable static state.
`new` call, `List` parameter, extending a class, shared mutable static state.
explanation: A parameter is data coupling, the weakest. A `new` call adds knowledge of how to build the collaborator, which is why moving it to the caller — dependency injection — removes half of it. Inheritance is stronger still, since you depend on internal calls nobody documented. Shared mutable static state is worst: everything touching it is coupled to everything else touching it, invisibly.
